Haploinsufficiency of NR0B1 disrupts its role in the regulation of gene expression, leading to distinct but related downstream phenotypic consequences contributing to monocytic leukemia (MONDO:0012902) and gingival fibromatosis (MONDO:0033493).

**How to falsify it:** The absence of pathogenic variants in NR0B1 in individuals with either MONDO:0012902 or fibromatosis, gingival, 5 would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, if pathogenic variants in NR0B1 are found to be loss-of-function in one disease and gain-of-function in the other, this would also falsify the proposed shared mechanism due to inconsistent functional directionality. _(variant: HGVS:c.XX_YYdel)_

**Why it matters:** Identifying NR0B1 as a shared causal gene for both MONDO:0012902 and fibromatosis, gingival, 5 could enable the development of targeted therapies that address the downstream consequences of NR0B1 dysregulation, potentially offering therapeutic benefit for both conditions.
